findings.finding: Extend the existing pay increase to calculate its effect on quartiles, fences and outlier status.
findings.breakdown: Students connect the movement of the observations and fences with unchanged IQR and outlier status.
findings.checked: The original quartiles are 490 and 680, giving IQR 190 and upper fence 965. After the increase, the quartiles are 510 and 700, the upper fence is 985, and the maximum is 990. All calculations use methods available by this topic.
findings.assumptions: Every employee receives the stated $20 increase.

repair.proposal: Append after p43-q10-b: (c) Find the new lower quartile. Answer: $510. (d) Find the new upper quartile. Answer: $700. (e) Find the new IQR. Answer: $190. (f) Find the new upper fence. Answer: $985. (g) Is the new highest wage an outlier? Explain why. Answer: yes; $990 exceeds $985.

protectedGroups.observation: Translating every value changes the median but preserves range and IQR.
Changing the maximum can change range without changing median or IQR.
Moving Q3 changes IQR while range and median remain fixed.
The median can change independently of range and IQR.
A narrower box can preserve the median and overall range.
protectedGroups.varies: Q1 increases from 3 to 4 and Q3 decreases from 7 to 6.

protectedGroups.observation: IQR depends on the labelled lower and upper quartiles, regardless of presentation order or additional statistics.
protectedGroups.varies: Values, order of givens and presence of irrelevant statistics.
protectedGroups.invariant: Select Q3 and Q1 and calculate Q3 − Q1.

protectedGroups.observation: Odd and even totals require different treatment of the overall median when forming the halves.
protectedGroups.varies: Dataset parity and whether the middle observation is excluded or the list splits directly into equal halves.
protectedGroups.invariant: Find each half's median and subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile.

protectedGroups.observation: Different cumulative proportions select different quartile boundaries on the same plot.
protectedGroups.varies: The finishing proportion changes from 50% to 75%.
protectedGroups.invariant: The male competitors, time scale and box plot.

protectedGroups.observation: The same numerical age interval can contain different proportions of different datasets, and combined counts must use the appropriate group totals.
protectedGroups.varies: The selected dataset, its quartile boundaries and its total.

protectedGroups.observation: The lower 75% ends at Q3, whereas the upper 75% starts at Q1.
protectedGroups.varies: Whether observations are below or above the requested boundary.

protectedGroups.observation: Reversing the tail reverses the direction of skew and the corresponding long whisker.
protectedGroups.varies: Direction of tail, longer whisker and median displacement.
protectedGroups.invariant: Aligned distribution curve and box-plot representation.

protectedGroups.observation: The same summary-to-plot procedure can produce symmetry or either direction of skew.
protectedGroups.invariant: Find the five-number summary, sketch the box plot, then classify.

protectedGroups.observation: The maximum range can be inferred first from numerical quartiles and then from IQR alone.
protectedGroups.varies: Specific quartiles are replaced by the width between them.
protectedGroups.invariant: Both endpoints can lie on the fences, giving a maximum range of four IQRs.
